newsitem.title: GERMANY: German rape-in-marriage ban clears last hurdle.
newsitem.headline: German rape-in-marriage ban clears last hurdle.

text.p: Germany's upper house of parliament passed a law on Friday making rape within marriage a criminal offence, clearing the last legal hurdle after wrangling on the issue that has lasted 25 years.
The new law, which finally brings Germany into line with most of its European Union partners, removes from the statute book a previous definition of rape as being extra-marital.

It redefines rape to include sexual abuse apart from forced penetration and makes rape of a man by either sex punishable. It also acknowledges that emotional as well physical violence could force someone into sex and sets a maximum jail sentence of 15 years for rape.
The law is the result of the fifth cross-party bill launched in parliament since 1972.
